content.reply:
Good fit for a small app: a food log you keep adding to, with daily calorie totals, day-by-day history and a trend chart. You type what you ate and how much, Alpha shows the calories, and you can correct any number. Two quick things before I write it up:

1. Should Alpha estimate calories from what you type, or will you enter the numbers yourself?
2. Calories only, or also protein, carbs and fat?

If you'd rather not decide: Alpha estimates calories (marked as estimates, editable) and tracks calories only.

interpretation.outcome: A small food log on your Mac where you record what you eat and how much, see calories per day, browse past days, and view trends over time.
interpretation.main_input: Short entries you type yourself, like "2 rotis and dal" or "large latte", with the amount.
interpretation.useful_result: Each entry saved with its calories, a running total for today, a day-by-day history, and a chart of daily calories over recent weeks.
important_assumptions: Alpha can estimate calories from your description, and you can correct any number.
Everything stays on this Mac; nothing is sent anywhere.

content.reply: Settled with defaults: Alpha estimates the calories from what you type, marks them as estimates, and you can overwrite any number. Calories only for now — protein, carbs and fat can be added later. So you'll get a quick-entry food log, today's running total, a day-by-day history you can browse, and a chart of daily calories for the last 7 and 30 days with your average. Everything stays on this Mac, and estimates come from the model, not from nutrition websites, so they're ballpark until you correct them. I'll write it up now.

build.goal: Keep a personal food log with amounts and calories, so the user can see today's total, look back at past days, and see how daily calories trend over time.
build.instructions:
App name for the person: Daily Food Log

What success looks like: The user can add a meal in a few seconds, see today's calorie total update, open any past day, and see a chart of daily calories for the last 7 and 30 days.

How the person will use it:
- Open the app and type what was eaten and how much, e.g. "2 rotis and dal, 1 bowl". -> A calorie figure appears for the entry, marked as an estimate, with the time filled in.
- Save the entry, or type your own calorie number first. -> The entry appears in today's list and today's calorie total updates.
- Tap an entry to fix the food, amount, time or calorie number, or delete it. -> The entry and the day's total update.
- Browse to an earlier day. -> That day's entries and total are shown.
- Open trends. -> A chart of daily calories for the last 7 and 30 days, with the daily average.

What it keeps:
- collection Food entries: One record per thing eaten, so days can be totalled and trends drawn.. Fields: When (datetime, required), Food (text, required), Amount (text, required), Calories (number, required), Calories are an estimate (boolean), Meal (choice)

What it does:
- action estimate_calories: Takes the food description and the amount and returns a calorie figure, clearly labelled as an estimate the user can overwrite. (inputs: food description, amount; outputs: estimated calories, estimate label)
- action log_entry: Saves the food, amount, time, calories and optional meal label as a new entry in the log. Uses the estimate unless the user typed a calorie number. (inputs: food description, amount, date and time, calories, meal label; outputs: saved entry, updated total for that day)
- action correct_entry: Lets the user change the food, amount, time, meal or calorie number of an existing entry, or remove it; totals recalculate and the estimate label is dropped when the user sets the number. (inputs: entry, changed values; outputs: updated entry, updated day total)
- action day_view: Lists all entries for a chosen day in time order, with that day's calorie total. (inputs: date; outputs: entry list, day total)
- action trends: Sums calories per day and shows the last 7 and 30 days as a chart with the daily average. (inputs: date range; outputs: daily totals, average per day)

Constraints:
- All entries stay on this Mac.
- Estimated calories must be visibly marked as estimates and always editable.
- No nutrition websites or apps are consulted; estimates come from the model only.
- Calories only; no protein, carbs or fat in the first version.

Agreed assumptions:
- Alpha estimates calories from your description and amount; the number is labelled an estimate and you can replace it with your own.
- The first version tracks calories only; protein, carbs and fat can be added later.
- Entries are timestamped now, and the date and time can be changed.
- Each entry can carry an optional meal label (breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack).
- Trends show daily calories for the last 7 and 30 days with the daily average.
- Daily goals, saved favourite foods, weekly summaries and reminders are left out of the first version.

PLAN.md is what Alpha will check. Where it names an action, input, collection, field or label differently from the notes above, use PLAN.md's name.

Build a screen for this App (ui/src/main.tsx) using the labels PLAN.md names.

scenarios.description: The person describes a lunch, gets an estimate marked as an estimate, saves the entry with their own calorie number, and today's list and total show it.
An entry saved without a typed calorie number is stored as an estimate; when the person sets the number, the stored calories change and the estimate flag is dropped.
Entries on yesterday and today are stored, a past day can be opened with its own total, trends returns daily totals and an average, and deleting an entry removes it from storage.
Saving with a blank amount is refused, because calories depend on the amount, and nothing is written to storage.

scenarios.description: The person describes a lunch, gets an estimate marked as an estimate, saves the entry with their own calorie number, and today's list and total show it.
An entry saved without a typed calorie number is stored as an estimate; when the person sets the number, the stored calories change and the estimate flag is dropped.
Entries on yesterday and today are stored, a past day can be opened with its own total, trends returns daily totals and an average, and deleting an entry removes it from storage.
Saving with a blank amount is refused, because calories depend on the amount, and nothing is written to storage.
